backlogged.summary: The new 127 rule looks only at the command's first program. A compound command such as `cd sub && jest` or `FOO=1 make && jest` whose later program is missing prints `jest: not found`, which does not name `cd`, so it is now a plain exit-127 failure rather than an environment stop. This follows the SPEC wording, but users of chained commands lose the environment-stop behaviour.

The built-in `harness ` execution is not used for repro commands or adapter CLIs, and `npx harness …` still goes through the shell. That is consistent with the SPEC, but the docs could say that only verify commands, checks and test_count are covered.

The firstProgram/commandNotFound tests run only with `platform: linux` or `win32` passed in. No end-to-end test exercises a real chained command, and the Windows cmd.exe path is still unit-only (related to B193).

conflictMarkedFiles uses lstat only on the final path component. A changed path whose parent directory is a symbolic link (e.g. 'dir/file' with 'dir' -> outside) would still be followed. git does not normally report paths beyond a symlink, so this is not reachable today; a realpath-inside-wt check would close it for good.

The built-in 'harness …' path runs this checkout's bin/harness.mjs. When verify runs from a feature worktree's own core, that means builder-modified core code runs as the verify command. This is the same trust as running the core itself (threat model D1), but a pinned core path for `harness run` would be worth documenting.

The new first-program 127 rule classifies compound commands such as 'cd sub && make' (with make missing) as a plain failure, because the first program is 'cd'. This matches SPEC §6.1 as written, but it changes environment-stop behaviour for such commands, and the change is not called out in docs/run.md.
The AC-3 test is skipped silently on Windows without symlink privilege (EPERM return), so Windows has no coverage of the lstat path.
